title: Поступок настоящего мужчины  (The Act of a Real Man)

segments.t: After Katya flees in tears, Eleonora emerges from the bathroom and tells Denis he acted like a real man by taking the blame on himself. Downstairs, Barinov comforts his heartbroken daughter while Denis wonders if he can still make things right.
Ты поступил как мужчина.
Спасибо тебе за молчание.
Бывают моменты, когда мы отчаянно злимся на самих себя из-за поступков,
которые мы совершили.
Из-за людей, которые счастливы без нас.
Катя, дочка моя!
Ты опять, да?
Катя? Опять?
Папа, мне очень плохо.
Из-за слов, которые сказали, не подумав.
Может, пора перестать себя ненавидеть и попытаться что-то исправить?
Хотя бы попытаться.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Ты поступил как мужчина.
'You acted like a man.' With the point and tears in play, Eleonora keeps this short reply brisk and direct. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Спасибо тебе за молчание.
'Thank you for keeping silent.' Over the point and the tears, Eleonora answers Barinov without a second thought. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Бывают моменты, когда мы отчаянно злимся на самих себя из-за поступков,

'There are moments when we are desperately angry at ourselves because of the deeds' Saying that there are moments when they are desperately angry at themselves because of the deeds is how Denis sets the tone with Barinov.
которые мы совершили.
'that we committed.' Around the point and tears, Denis sets a calm, everyday tone with Barinov.
Из-за людей, которые счастливы без нас.
'Because of the people who are happy without us.' Adding that because of the people who are happy without them fills in the missing piece for Barinov.
Катя, дочка моя!
'Katya, my daughter!' Over the tears and the kitchen, Barinov lets his real feelings show.
Ты опять, да?
'You are drinking again, huh?' Wondering if Denis is drinking again huh shows Barinov caught off guard. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Катя? Опять?
'Katya? Again?' With the tears and moment hanging in the air, Barinov puts Denis on the spot. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Папа, мне очень плохо.
'Dad, I feel terrible.' Barinov reminds Denis that dad he feels terrible before the moment passes.
Из-за слов, которые сказали, не подумав.
'Because of the words we spoke without thinking.' Because because of the words they spoke without thinking, Denis treats the matter as settled.
Может, пора перестать себя ненавидеть и попытаться что-то исправить?

'Maybe it is time to stop hating ourselves and try to fix something?' Asking whether maybe it is time to stop hating themselves and try to fix something puts Barinov right on the defensive. Russian packs the whole idea of what is allowed or needed into one impersonal word at the front.
Хотя бы попытаться.
'At least try.' With the truth and tears in play, Denis keeps this short reply brisk and direct. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

которые мы совершили.

Ты опять, да?

Из-за слов, которые сказали, не подумав.
Может, пора перестать себя ненавидеть и попытаться что-то исправить?
Хотя бы попытаться.
And that brings this scene at the hotel to a close. Listen out for how Eleonora and the team handle the pressure when you watch the episode. See you next time!
Пока!
